statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-80231: libcurl can wrongly reuse an existing HTTPS connection to a host for a transfer that uses a different native CA store setting (CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA) than the one the connection was set up with (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-80231.html). curl lists it as affecting 7.71.0 through 8.21.0, fixed it in curl 8.22.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/7be1e70cb6bcd83e130ecfe8cb91b6a7dcdeff42, and states that the bug exists only on Windows and macOS. The native CA store option only changes which certificates libcurl trusts when libcurl uses the Windows certificate store or Apple's SecTrust, code that curl compiles only for those platforms (the USE_WIN32_CRYPTO and USE_APPLE_SECTRUST blocks in its TLS code, visible in the fix). The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 (8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0 (in both the main and the security repository), 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, on x86_64 and aarch64) are Linux builds of libcurl using OpenSSL 3 (every libcurl build links libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3), where setting or clearing CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA does not change the trust store, so reusing a connection across the two settings exposes nothing. The affected code path is not reachable on these builds; builds from 8.22.0-r0 also carry the upstream fix.
